_about.frame: panel 1920 x 720, x right, y down. The model takes OpenCV pixel-centre panel coordinates (= continuous - 0.5), like tools/overlay/rectify.py and tools/g20spec/zoom.py.
_about.entries: <id>: the global model (whole panel): `model` (homography + radial k1, what zoom.py reads) plus `field`, a smooth residual correction the rasters include. <id>_strip: the zoom.py form only, refitted on the control points in the lower half (y >= 400, k1 held): the best plain model for the STRIP when the field cannot be used (zoom.py --hjson this file --photo <id>_strip).
_about.zoom_py_offset: tools/g20spec/zoom.py samples crop pixel k at OpenCV panel x0 + k/n, i.e. continuous x0 + k/n + 0.5: its crop pixel k is NOT centred at continuous x0 + (k + .5)/n; the difference is (n - 1)/(2n) panel px (0.44 px at n = 8). The rasters of package R are centred.
_about.residuals: rms / max in panel px over the inlier control points (true panel point vs photo point mapped back by the model); *_strip = the same over control points with y >= 520; loo = leave-one-out.
_about.chain: 60 is absolute (our grid). Every other photo is tied to 60's rect through BMW content that never moves (dial scales, rails, minis), so all share 60's frame.
